rules.scope: infer a temporal semantic type from a bounded column sample when at least 80 percent of non-null strings match a registered calendar or timestamp morphology and at least two distinct values parse
rules.rationale: Physical string type does not determine visualization semantic type; timestamp morphology is positive evidence even when a producer omits the separator between an ISO date and time.
rules.failure_condition: A date or timestamp column is treated as categorical solely because its serialized representation is non-standard but deterministically parseable.
rules.conflict_policy: Existing temporal types win; numeric identifiers are excluded; morphology and parse thresholds must both pass; profiling never rewrites source values.

rules.scope: classify every field-resolution evidence item as explicit grounding, semantic grounding, schema inference, contextual support, or weak overlap
rules.rationale: Lexical observations, schema-derived inferences, and task-conditioned compatibility have different epistemic force and must not be interchangeable in required-field decisions.
rules.failure_condition: A schema inference or contextual compatibility signal is treated as equivalent to a query-grounded field mention.
rules.conflict_policy: The classification is immutable and auditable; it does not change candidate scores by itself and unknown evidence types default to contextual support.

rules.scope: remove a required-field obligation only when all of its query-grounded token support is owned by one or more stronger explicit field mentions and no independent complete mention remains
rules.rationale: A weak phrase window may cross two complete mentions, so ownership must be decided token by token rather than by requiring one owner span to contain the entire window.
rules.failure_condition: A phrase such as convex area across grain class creates an extra grain-area obligation because a weak window combines tokens owned by convex-area and grain-class mentions.
rules.conflict_policy: Any independent complete explicit, alias, acronym, value, or semantic mention preserves the obligation; schema inference and contextual support cannot defeat explicit multi-owner coverage.

rules.scope: map unsupported governing-operation lexemes to a versioned canonical label while preserving the matched lexical form and span
rules.rationale: Forecast and prediction are related but distinct requested operations; an explicit predict verb must not be relabeled as forecast merely because future scope is also present.
rules.failure_condition: A query safely abstains but reports a canonical unsupported-operation label inconsistent with its governing verb.
rules.conflict_policy: Explicit forecast lexemes map to forecast; explicit predict lexemes map to prediction even with future modifiers; project plus future scope maps to forecast; field-grounded spans are excluded before classification.
